solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Reviewed bistrot/cafe La Maison: sandwiches "criminal"

indicators.note: viewed again from the other end, so the hidden run of letters is read backwards
the phrase holds the letters between its outer parts, as bread holds a filling

explanation.surface: A restaurant critic's write-up of a French bistro accuses its sandwiches of being criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' finds ROTCAFELAM across 'bistrot/cafe La Maison', and 'Reviewed' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a wrongdoer or offender is someone criminal, used here as a noun.

clue.text: Somewhat hormonal, Isabella is an enigmatic figure

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these two words are used, a run spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: Someone with a hormonal temperament, Isabella is hard to read, a mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo's portrait is famous for its sitter's enigmatic smile, making her the classic enigmatic figure.

clue.text: See 1
Didn't Trump go after journalist with court case?

parts.note: to go after someone is to follow them
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's stock journalist
a lawsuit is a court case

explanation.surface: A political question: didn't President Trump pursue a reporter through the courts?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump' looks like the US president; in card games, to trump is to play a trump card, while following suit means playing a card of the suit led.
explanation.definitionFit: In card play, following suit means playing the suit led instead of trumping it; the idiom means copying others.

clue.text: Old Bill gathered wood

indicators.note: 'I gathered' means I heard, so the word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: the Old Bill is British slang for the police, the cops

explanation.surface: The police collected firewood, or a man named Bill picked up some timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered' looks like collecting; here it means 'heard', the sound signal. 'Old Bill' is British slang for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A small group of trees, a thicket, is a little wood.

clue.text: Hirsute character in Oxford University called Brown

indicators.note: the word for telephoned sits inside the abbreviations for the university

parts.note: O is an abbreviation for Oxford
to have called someone on the phone is to have rang them, past tense rang
tan is a shade of brown

explanation.surface: A shaggy-haired figure at Oxford, named Brown, sounds like a don.
explanation.definitionFit: This great ape is covered in long reddish hair, so it is a hirsute, or hairy, creature.

clue.text: Steer clear of wildcat general strike; it's a tragedy eerst

indicators.note: the answer is what remains of the fodder once it is free of the letters of the first word
a wildcat strike is unofficial and disorderly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, its letters are the ones to be removed

explanation.surface: Advice to keep away from an unofficial nationwide stoppage: it would be a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of GENERAL STRIKE, less those of STEER, are rearranged ('clear of', 'wildcat'). The stray 'eerst' at the end is a typesetting gremlin the setter confirmed on the blog, not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's play about an old monarch and his three daughters is one of his great tragedies.

clue.text: In European empty bar I had dinner date resembling Edna

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its contents, leaving just its first and last letters

parts.note: to have had dinner is to have eaten, ate

explanation.surface: A European bar where I dined with a date, a place like Edna's.
explanation.walkthrough: Edna, the Inebriate Woman was a celebrated 1971 BBC Play for Today about a homeless alcoholic woman, played by Patricia Hayes.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of a famous BBC television play calls its heroine Edna drunk, so being drunk is like Edna.

clue.text: Rustic logs chopped for those making camp fire?

indicators.note: logs that are chopped are cut into pieces, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Rough country logs are split for a group building a fire at camp.
explanation.definitionFit: Young members of the guiding movement go camping and learn to light a campfire, so they make camp fires.

clue.text: New salary caps not introduced at work; it gets up my nose

indicators.note: the letters are put to work, set in motion and rearranged
the word is not allowed its introduction, its first letter, which is dropped

explanation.surface: A grumble about new pay limits at the office: it really irritates me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not introduced' takes C from CAPS, leaving APS, which joins SALARY for 'at work' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A decongestant spray is literally squirted up the nose, while 'gets up my nose' is British idiom for annoys.

clue.text: See 6
Names US mountains as stated by Yankee

indicators.note: the word is said the way an American might pronounce it, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: the Appalachians are a mountain range in the eastern United States

explanation.surface: An American lists the names of the mountains of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: An appellation is a title or designation, a formal synonym for a name.

clue.text: Live like a king with dad in castles in far-flung places

indicators.note: the ruling word and the father word go within the fortifications

parts.note: castles are forts, strongholds
a king reigns, so to live like one is to reign
pa is an informal word for dad

explanation.surface: Living royally with your father among castles in distant lands.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for abroad, distant overseas countries, is a stock phrase for far-flung places.

clue.text: Let rip guff; foul smell gets up one's nose!

indicators.note: foul suggests something messed up or rotten, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A lavatorial picture: someone breaks wind, and the stink assaults the nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guff' is British slang for breaking wind, which colours the surface. The definition describes the animal: the smell of truffles is what it sniffs out.
explanation.definitionFit: A hog trained to sniff out buried fungi works entirely by the scent that gets into its snout.

clue.text: Piece of ebony ruler?

parts.note: ebony is a deep black colour
a queen is a female ruler

explanation.surface: A question about a carving made from dark wood depicting a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of ebony ruler' reads like a historical figure or a carved object; 'Piece' alone is the definition, a chessman.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, one of the dark side's pieces is its most powerful one, the dark lady.

clue.text: Got up and prepared the pizza base

definitions.meaning: ... of bed, that is, got up in the morning
dough is flattened with a rolling pin to make a pizza base

explanation.surface: Someone got out of bed and made dough for a pizza.
explanation.definitionFit: One phrase covers both leaving bed sluggishly and flattening dough with a rolling pin.

clue.text: Not for the first time, falls over, leaving artist to support old morthern church

indicators.note: in a down clue the lower part supports, so it is placed after the upper part

parts.note: a typo for northern, abbreviated N
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: the painter's letters leave the reversed name, which loses them
turned over, the waterfall's name is read backwards

parts.note: Niagara is the most famous falls
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A clumsy person falls over again, and an artist props up an old church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falls over' gives ARAGAIN; 'leaving artist' takes RA out, and 'to support' puts the remainder below O N CE. 'morthern' is a slip for 'northern'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something once more means it is happening again, a repeat, so not the first time.

clue.text: She's an inspiration for occasionally weird author

indicators.note: only now and then, every other letter, is taken from the words

explanation.surface: A muse inspiring an eccentric writer from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the Greek Muse of love poetry, and the Muses were the inspiration of artists.

clue.text: Heads of Foreign Office committee unusually struggle to concentrate …

indicators.note: the heads of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Senior figures on a Foreign Office committee find it oddly hard to pay attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To focus is to concentrate attention on something, a direct synonym.

clue.text: … as multiple channels stream Tory with excellent oratory skills

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, the Tory party
a fluent speaker is articulate

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a Tory talks smoothly while many TV channels broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'channels stream' suggests broadcasting; here it is rivers whose channels flow together.
explanation.definitionFit: Watercourses that flow into one another and merge are described as confluent, so streams converging.

clue.text: Design squalid sites as means to raise quick cash?

indicators.note: to design is to plan a new layout, so the letters are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A developer plans run-down plots as a way of making fast money.
explanation.definitionFit: Holdings easily turned into money, such as cash in the bank or shares, are what one sells to raise funds fast.

clue.text: Composer putting note in envelope (no stamp required)

indicators.note: the note is put inside the envelope

parts.note: an SAE is a stamped addressed envelope, so the sender needs no stamp
ti is a note in the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A musician posting a note in a reply-paid envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: An SAE, a stamped addressed envelope, is a British convenience: you send one so the reply costs the replier nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Erik is the French writer of the Gymnopédies, a piano music maker, so a composer.

clue.text: Book a month to take over from glum donkey

parts.note: Jan is short for January

indicators.note: to take something away removes it from the word
says which word the letter is taken out of

parts.note: Eeyore is the gloomy donkey in Winnie-the-Pooh
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A calendar month takes the place of a miserable donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take over from' reads as replacement, but 'over' is O, taken from EEYORE, the gloomy donkey of A. A. Milne's Pooh stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte Brontë's novel is a famous book.

clue.text: See 22
Suites arranged to suit Norwegian's booking?

definitions.text: Suites arranged to suit Norwegian's booking?

parts.words: Suites arranged to suit Norwegian's booking?
parts.note: Grieg's two orchestral suites were arranged from his music for Ibsen's play, a Norwegian's work

explanation.surface: Hotel suites set up to meet a Norwegian guest's reservation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suites' and 'booking' suggest a hotel; the suites are Grieg's, drawn from his incidental music for a play by the Norwegian Ibsen.
explanation.definitionFit: Grieg wrote incidental music for Ibsen's verse drama and arranged it into two famous orchestral suites.

clue.text: Like the tale of bird fencing Romeo's mate's stolen car?

indicators.note: a fence encloses, so the bird's letters surround the rest

parts.note: the canary is a songbird

indicators.note: when the vehicle is stolen it is taken away from the friend's name

parts.note: Mercutio is Romeo's friend in Shakespeare's play
a Merc is a Mercedes car

explanation.surface: A story of a bird guarding a getaway car belonging to Romeo's friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fencing' also hints at swordplay, apt for Mercutio, who dies in a duel. Taking MERC from MERCUTIO leaves UTIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Belloc's Cautionary Tales are warning stories, so such a tale is one meant as a warning.

clue.text: See 24
Fake uni degrees heavily attacked

indicators.note: fake qualifications are made up, so the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: Bogus university degrees come in for heavy criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: A town besieged is surrounded and bombarded by an army, so heavily attacked.
